lockedFeatures: three-quarter-front orientation of the trouser waist
exactly ONE square-ended button tab on the waistband at the side, fully fastened
exactly ONE button, sewn at the forward end of the tab and engaged through it
square/rectangular tab and keeper with topstitched outline (not rounded, not pointed)
no belt loops, no buckle, no D-ring, no hook, no second adjuster
forward pleats falling from the waistband on the trouser front
jetted (besom) slant hip pocket below and behind the adjuster
solid navy fine-wool trouser cloth with visible weave
zero text, numbers, arrows, leader lines, red marks or any annotation
notes: Attempt 2. Attempt 1 was rejected for frame dominance only; the framing correction worked without regressing any geometry. Blueprint fidelity remains exact: three-quarter front trouser waist; ONE square button-tab adjuster on the waistband at the side, fully fastened, with exactly ONE button at the forward end and a squared keeper strap running back, reproducing the drawing's left-to-right arrangement (front pleats -> side adjuster -> jetted hip pocket). The red band in the illustration is position notation and is correctly rendered in the garment's own navy cloth; no red, no annotation, no text anywhere. Attempt 2 removed the shirt, the thigh, the knee, the leg and any pose from frame and brought the camera in; the tab now spans about 44% of the frame width and is the only detail in the upper half, so the option is identifiable in well under a second. Composition is scored against the intent of the 40-60% dominance target rather than a literal area percentage: a side adjuster sits on the waistband, which is a full-width line across the garment, and magnifying a thin tab to 40-60% of frame AREA would destroy the waistband context that makes it legible as a side adjuster rather than a belt loop or pocket tab. Catalog copy says 'Square button adjusters on both sides' while the option id is adjuster-left; a three-quarter front view can only show one side and the drawing highlights one side, so the single visible adjuster is faithful and no fault is recorded.
